name: Timeline

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code:
<>
  <Title as="h2" textSize="5">
    Order history
  </Title>
  <Timeline titleAs="h3">
    <Timeline.Item
      title="Delivered"
      time="16 October 2026, 11:40"
      dateTime="2026-10-16T11:40"
      color="success"
    >
      Signed for by A. Smith.
    </Timeline.Item>
    <Timeline.Item
      title="Shipped"
      time="14 October 2026, 08:12"
      dateTime="2026-10-14T08:12"
    >
      <Paragraph>
        Tracking number <Link href="#track">1Z999AA10123456784</Link>
      </Paragraph>
    </Timeline.Item>
    <Timeline.Item
      title="Order placed"
      time="12 October 2026, 09:30"
      dateTime="2026-10-12T09:30"
    />
  </Timeline>
</>

examples.title: A Timeline That Changes
Compound (dot-notation) usage

accessibility:
- **A list:** it's an `<ol>`, since a timeline's order is its meaning, with `role="list"`. Safari
  stops treating a list as one once its numbers are hidden, and the role keeps it a list there, so
  a screen reader says how many events there are and where each one is.
- **Headings:** each title is a heading, `h2` unless `titleAs` says otherwise, so screen reader
  users can move from event to event. Pick the level under the heading the timeline sits beneath:
  an `h3` under an `h2`. In a busy feed, `titleAs="p"` makes them plain lines.
- **States in words and shapes:** the current item has `aria-current="step"`. A completed item's
  title ends with "completed", an upcoming one's with "upcoming", and the pending one's with "in
  progress", in visually hidden text, so its heading reads "Packed completed". Set the words in
  your app's language with `completedLabel`, `upcomingLabel` and `pendingLabel`. Each state has a
  shape of its own as well as a color.
- **Decoration:** the markers are hidden from assistive tech, an `Icon` with an `ariaLabel`
  included, and the line is drawn by CSS. Say what a color or an icon means in the title.
- **The time:** a screen reader mostly reads the text, so the time's words carry the whole date.
  `dateTime` puts the same moment in a `<time datetime>` for machines, and for the readers that
  speak it.
- **Motion:** the pending ring turns, and stands still for users who ask for less motion. Its open
  shape is the cue either way.
- **Forced colors:** every line, dot, ring and halo is a border or an outline, so in Windows high
  contrast mode they keep their shapes, and the pending ring stays open.
- **Not interactive and not live:** it has no tab stop and no keys, and links or buttons in an
  item work as they do anywhere. It announces nothing when it changes, so keep a status region
  beside one that changes on screen, as in [A Timeline That Changes](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/timeline#a-timeline-that-changes).
- **A record first:** design systems with user research behind them, the UK's
  [MOJ](https://design-patterns.service.justice.gov.uk/components/timeline/) and
  [HMRC](https://design.tax.service.gov.uk/hmrc-design-patterns/timeline/), use a timeline for a
  record and advise against using one as a progress indicator. That's why a record is the default.
  `active` is for something that moves on its own and is only reported to the user. For a journey
  the user moves through, where they may go back, use [`Steps`](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/steps).
summary: The `Timeline` component renders a list of events in the order they happened, each with a marker on a line down the side. By default it's a record, an order's history, a ticket's activity or a changelog, and it marks nothing. With `active` it marks progress, for something that moves along on its own and is reported to the user: a parcel, a deployment, a claim. That reads oldest first, and `pending` ends it on what's under way. A journey the user moves through themselves, like a wizard or a checkout, is `Steps`. It's an `<ol role="list">`, so it stays a list in Safari with its numbers hidden, and each title is a heading at the level `titleAs` sets. The markers are decoration and hidden from assistive tech, so the states are read as words: `aria-current="step"` on the current item, and "completed", "upcoming" or "in progress" after the other titles, in the language the label props set. Nothing here is a control or a live region, so a timeline that changes on screen keeps a `role="status"` region beside it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: children
props.description: `Timeline.Item`s, in the order they're read: newest first or oldest first for a record, oldest first with `active` or `pending`.

props.name: active
props.description: Marks progress. The item at this index, counting the children from 0, is current; the ones before it are completed and the ones after it are upcoming. Leave it out for a record, where nothing is marked. `-1` marks every item upcoming, and an index past the last marks them all completed. Each child counts as one item, with Fragments and arrays opened up, so render one item per child. A component of your own around a `Timeline.Item` still gets its state, but one that renders nothing still counts.

props.name: pending
props.description: What's under way, as a last item after the children: its title, read with `pendingLabel`. Write it as words that say so ("Out for delivery").

props.name: align
props.description: `start`: the rail at the start of the line. `end`: at the end, with the text against it. `alternate`: down the middle, the items taking turns and each time across the rail; below Bulma's tablet breakpoint it's `start`.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: What every item's title renders as: a heading at the level under the heading the timeline sits beneath, or `p` for a busy feed.

props.name: color
props.description: The markers' color, and the color of progress with `active`. Neutral without it, and Bulma's `link` for progress. The markers are hidden from assistive tech, so say what a color means in the words too.

props.name: completedLabel
props.description: Read after a completed item's title, visually hidden. In your app's language.

props.name: upcomingLabel
props.description: Read after an upcoming item's title, visually hidden. In your app's language.

props.name: pendingLabel
props.description: Read after the pending item's title, visually hidden. In your app's language.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.

parts.catchAll: All standard <ol> attributes and Bulma helper props

parts.summary: One event: a marker on the rail, then its title, its time and anything else about it. Outside a `Timeline` it's a record item with an `h2` title, though the styles are registered on `.timeline`, so the rail and the marker need one.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes to apply.

props.name: title
props.description: What happened, in a line. It renders as the root's `titleAs`.

props.name: time
props.description: When it happened, as the reader sees it: "14 October 2026", "2 hours ago". Put the whole date in the words, since screen readers mostly read the text.

props.name: dateTime
props.description: The same moment for machines, as HTML's `datetime` takes it: "2026-10-14", "2026-10-14T08:12", "2026-10". With it, `time` renders in a `<time>`. Keep it the same moment as `time`, since some readers speak it.

props.name: icon
props.description: A picture in the marker. A string is an `Icon` name, drawn from the icon library `ConfigProvider` sets, and anything else renders as it is. Without it, the marker is a dot. It's hidden from assistive tech, so what it means goes in the title.

props.name: color
props.description: This item's marker color, over the root's. Say what it means in the words too.

props.name: children
props.description: Anything else about the event, under the title and the time, as written.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Text color helper.

props.name: bgColor
props.description: Background color helper.
